source.title: Fact Finding: Attempting to Reverse-Engineer Factual Recall on the Neuron Level (Post 1)

record.file_problem: None; the full post, including its summaries of the linked posts, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses superposition and reports experiments on factual recall, but does not directly test the listed versions’ claims about sparse overcomplete features, capacity pressure, SAE feature completeness, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The post reports results about linear recoverability of athlete sports and individual-neuron behavior. These do not directly measure the feature overlap, sparsity-dependent geometry, capacity allocation, SAE properties, or dimensionality named by the claim versions, so the rows are linked to none. Statements about SAE results from other work are cited evidence and are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The post is framed around superposition, which it assumes as motivation. Its results are about factual-recall circuitry in Pythia 2.8B: linear recoverability of sport, neuron-ablation correlations, and one non-monosemantic neuron. None measures feature overlap, capacity allocation, SAE properties or feature dimensionality. The claim that lookup is not localisable to specific neurons concerns circuit distribution, not feature counts versus dimensions. The SAE remarks are cited work and speculation; the authors did not train SAEs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Add three points: the authors judge that they fell short of mechanistically understanding computation in superposition, they treat early MLPs as an uninterpretable lookup table best black-boxed, and they call this a downward update on ambitious full reverse-engineering.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies factual recall in Pythia rather than reproducing the original toy-model setup.

fits_no_version.finding: A classifier built from L16H20's output directions predicts athlete sport with 86% accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity attributes are linearly recoverable in early-mid residual streams (multi-token embeddings).

fits_no_version.finding: Probe accuracy for sport rises gradually through MLPs 2–4, with no clean hashing stage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fact lookup is spread across several MLP layers rather than staged cleanly.

fits_no_version.finding: Effects of single-neuron resample ablation correlate little across different facts about Michael Jordan.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different facts about one entity rely on different neuron sets, against single-step detokenization.

fits_no_version.finding: L5N6045 fires more for baseball players, even on orthogonalised components, yet is not monosemantic on broader data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-relevant MLP neurons in factual recall are partially specialised but polysemantic.

record.problems: The authors note that the analysis covers 1,500 facts while each of the five studied MLP layers had 10,000 neurons, making it underdetermined. Several summarized findings are qualitative, and the post says the authors did not explore SAEs themselves.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Statements cited from other work, including SAE findings, were excluded.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model of sparse features versus dimensions. The toy memorisation models in Post 4 are not reported with results here.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or decides dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure. L5N6045 is described only as not monosemantic, with no cause tested.
Whether features are spread across more neurons than dimensions allow, or recovered by SAEs. The SAE evidence is cited, not produced.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
Dimensionality of superposed features. The sport is described as a linear subspace, but 1-D versus multi-D is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is Post 1 of a 5-post sequence and mostly summarises Posts 2–5. Several results appear only qualitatively (known vs unknown name MLP norms, breaking linear structure, Post 5 context-truncation cosine similarities). None bears on a claim version. The 1,500 facts against 10,000 neurons per layer is an acknowledged underdetermination.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure, or whether it is evidence for superposition.
Whether features are spread across many neurons or recoverable as sparse SAE features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the investigation and is discussed extensively, but its cataloged claim versions are not directly tested or used as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: The reported results test factual-recall mechanisms and specific detokenization hypotheses; they do not establish feature overlap, capacity-driven polysemanticity, dictionary properties, or feature dimensionality.

source_check.notes: The authors report falling short of mechanistically understanding computation in superposition. Their speculation about SAE usefulness is explicitly untested; they did not explore SAEs.
